title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault‑Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor‑CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled‑challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled‑fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per preregistered rules). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier‑guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded‑only), n01 = 1 (baseline‑only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two‑sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired‑bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt‑5‑mini and recorded 118 hosted‑model calls (budget 120). A preregistered confirmatory harmful‑overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor; the frozen harmful‑change mapping and per‑episode traces required to compute it are archived and their locations are provided in Methods. We report confirmatory results, document reproducibility artifacts, and treat the preregistered harmful‑overrepair hypothesis as unresolved in the confirmatory summary while preserving all audited evidence for independent recomputation.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent‑to‑configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety‑oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): a candidate configuration is checked by a deterministic verifier and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are exposed to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior empirical work in code and Infrastructure‑as‑Code (IaC) settings shows deterministic verifier interposition can raise verifier‑detected pass rates while also exposing new failure modes and imposing interaction costs [1]–[3]. Survey and field studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps likewise emphasize that read‑oriented usefulness does not automatically imply safe closed‑loop execution without conservative verification and orchestration [5].

Motivation and research question. Controlled paired evidence that measures the causal effect of exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair loop on vendor CLI templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse. A central methodological concern is intervention informativeness: a verifier‑guided intervention can affect outcomes only when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics. We therefore ran a preregistered deterministic controlled‑fault challenge (outcome‑independent assignment) in a paired design that reuses the identical controlled‑fault candidate across arms. Our research question (preregistered): Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor‑CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work:
Empirical GVR evidence is concentrated in program repair, IaC, and DSL domains. Controlled evaluations show that inserting deterministic verifiers between generation and acceptance and supplying verifier diagnostics to a repair model can improve verifier pass rates on those task families [1], [2]. Work studying iterative refinement cautions that single‑proxy verifiers can be exploited by optimization toward the proxy (verifier‑exploitation) unless mitigations are applied [3]. Studies instrumenting multi‑step pipelines also report a measurable ‘verifier tax’—increased interaction steps and compute cost—when verifiers are interposed [4].

Survey and field literature in NetOps/AIOps report that LLMs are often useful for diagnosis and documentation but warn that moving to autonomous, closed‑loop changes requires robust verification, coverage analysis, and deployment‑level validation [5]. These strands motivated our preregistered controlled‑challenge paired design: deterministic faults to ensure intervention activation, shared‑candidate pairing that isolates the effect of diagnostics under the adapter semantics used, and frozen scoring/harmful‑change mappings to make safety aggregations auditable.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where the binary success predicate requires both the deterministic vendor‑CLI validator and a simulator‑based compliance agreement (verifier+simulator). The preregistration SHA‑256 is recorded in the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = 0ba66573928647f008b2cd5b9dde6708a61ae86ece55b693ace534e01e2b132c).

Design, adapter semantics, and sampling. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index a single deterministically injected controlled‑fault candidate (deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1) was produced and reused unchanged across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one initial generation (shared) and one repair opportunity per condition; baseline = blind repair (no diagnostics exposed), guarded = repair with deterministic verifier diagnostics exposed. The adapter‑mandated confirmatory task_count was fixed at 40 in the preregistration.

Model and runtime sampling records. The archived model configuration declares declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini and temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json. Null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Per‑call runtime sampling parameters and provider call metadata are archived in the execution artifacts (for example, execution/raw_results.jsonl and the provider call traces under execution/provider_calls/) and summarized in the execution manifest; auditors may consult those archived per‑call records to inspect sampling details and call ordering. The runtime provider call accounting in the execution manifest records hosted model call usage (hosted_model_call_event_count = 118; maximum_model_calls = 120).

Controlled‑challenge sampling and missingness rules. To ensure intervention activation we preregistered 40 deterministic controlled faults (task indices 1..40). The execution manifest reports source_generation_attempt_count = 40, source_valid_count = 39, source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1. The preregistered missingness rule 'complete_pair_primary' excludes a pair from the primary analysis only if both condition executions for that pair are unscorable; this occurred once and is documented in analysis/missingness_summary.csv.

Scoring rules, harmful‑change mapping, and reproducibility. The primary success predicate is verifier+simulator agreement computed by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and the simulator check. The preregistration froze a harmful‑change labeling mapping used for the preregistered harmful‑overrepair hypothesis. Compact operational mapping (as implemented in the archived transformation artifact): label an episode harmful if its validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE. The transformation artifact and per‑episode validator traces required to compute the preregistered harmful‑overrepair aggregation are archived (see execution/transformation_manifest.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, and the per‑episode scoring JSON files under execution/scoring/); the confirmatory analysis executor archived with the study did not compute that preregistered harmful‑overrepair aggregation (see Results). Reproduction of the preregistered harmful‑overrepair statistic is deterministic from the archived artifacts and the compact mapping above; exact artifact locations are provided so auditors can recompute the preregistered statistic without ambiguity.

Statistical analysis plan. The preregistered primary test is an exact paired binary test (two‑sided McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired binomial). We report discordant‑pair counts, absolute paired risk difference, two‑sided exact p‑value, and a 95% paired‑bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Multiplicity: single predefined primary test; subgroup analyses are exploratory with CIs only. Missingness sensitivity analyses were preregistered: the primary analysis excludes incomplete pairs per 'complete_pair_primary'; a sensitivity analysis treats missing episodes as failures and is reported alongside the primary result.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs) with failed_episode_count = 2. Hosted model calls used = 118 (<= maximum 120). Source generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Run timestamps are recorded in the execution manifest (started_at_utc = 2026‑09‑04T21:16:50.730326+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026‑09‑04T21:19:34.370550+00:00). Stage counts in the provider audit are: valid_source_generation = 40; blind_controlled_fault_repair = 39; validator_guided_controlled_fault_repair = 39.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier‑guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded‑only), n01 = 1 (baseline‑only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two‑sided paired test (McNemar exact) p = 0.021484375. 95% paired‑bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The analysis artifacts analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv are archived and their SHA‑256 hashes are recorded in the evidence bundle.

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded under the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule because its source generation was invalid/unscorable; both condition episodes for that pair are unscorable (both_missing_pairs = 1). The missingness summary and per‑episode terminal error reasons are archived (analysis/missingness_summary.csv; execution/execution_log.jsonl; execution/raw_results.jsonl).

Preregistered harmful‑overrepair aggregation: archived status. The preregistration specified a confirmatory harmful‑overrepair hypothesis (guarded should not increase harmful over‑repairs beyond a prespecified threshold). The archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute that preregistered aggregation (secondary_results = []). Because the preregistered statistic was not produced in the archived confirmatory summary, we do not present a retroactive preregistered confirmatory safety claim. The frozen harmful‑change mapping and per‑episode validator_trace.violation_codes required to compute that aggregation are archived (execution/transformation_manifest.json; execution/scoring/*.json; execution/raw_results.jsonl). We therefore expose the exact reproducibility path (mapping + archived per‑episode traces) for independent recomputation; any numerical harmful‑overrepair counts computed outside the archived confirmatory summary are exploratory unless recomputed and recorded into the archive following the preregistered pipeline.

Representative diagnostic examples (archived). Representative per‑pair scoring JSON artifacts are archived (execution/scoring/task‑000001‑*.json, task‑000002‑*.json, task‑000003‑*.json, etc.). Example: pair‑000001 (fault_class = dropped_required_restore) shows both baseline and guarded repairs valid after repair and validator_feedback_exposed_to_model = true for the guarded episode. Example: pair‑000003 (protected_interface_change) shows baseline repair left PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE violations while guarded repair removed those violations and produced a valid configuration. These per‑episode traces illustrate concrete corrective edits driven by diagnostics and are archived for inspection.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The archived confirmatory evidence shows that, on the preregistered synthetic controlled‑fault bank and under the adapter's shared controlled‑fault pairing semantics, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to the repair model produced a substantial and statistically detectable increase in verifier+simulator‑validated outcomes (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.02148). The shared‑candidate paired design isolates the effect of exposing diagnostics because both arms received the identical initial controlled‑fault candidate and identical repair budgets; differences therefore reflect diagnostic exposure and subsequent repair behavior rather than different initial generations.

Mechanism and concrete traces. Archived per‑episode validator traces show that diagnostics commonly exposed the specific violation codes (e.g., PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE, FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH) and contextual state that enabled targeted corrective edits in guarded repairs. These traces provide a plausible causal pathway from diagnostic exposure to improved post‑repair verifier outcomes without requiring additional first‑pass generations.

Safety boundary and unresolved preregistered safety aggregation. We emphasize that the preregistered confirmatory harmful‑overrepair statistic was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor; the preregistered harmful‑change mapping and the traces necessary to compute it are archived and reproducible, and we provide the exact mapping above to enable deterministic recomputation by auditors. Because the confirmatory analysis omitted that preregistered aggregation, we do not upgrade any exploratory recomputation into a confirmatory safety verdict in this paper.

Operational implications and verifier tax. The verifier‑guided workflow incurred additional model–verifier interaction: the execution manifest records 118 hosted‑model calls and stage counts for each pipeline phase. These counts permit exploratory computation of model‑call cost per avoided failure but do not alone justify deployment‑scale cost/latency claims. Practitioners should weigh verifier coverage, verifier fidelity to real devices, and the interaction budget when considering deployment. The archived artifacts support follow‑up cost/latency studies.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: runtime sampling nondeterminism (temperature = null/unset) and exactly one initial sampled generation per pair limit claims about deterministic generation effects; differences across arms arise from diagnostics under the adapter contract. Construct validity: primary success depends on verifier+simulator agreement and thus on verifier coverage and simulator fidelity. External validity: confirmatory execution used a single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and a synthetic task bank; results do not establish multi‑model or broad production generality. Conclusion validity: with complete_pairs = 39 the primary contrast estimate has acceptable precision for the observed effect size but limited power for fine‑grained per‑fault‑class inference; subgroup analyses are exploratory.
sections.conclusion:
In this preregistered controlled‑challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled‑fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow substantially increased verifier+simulator‑validated configuration success on the tested synthetic bank (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This finding is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered confirmatory harmful‑overrepair test was not executed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; the per‑episode traces and frozen harmful‑change mapping required to compute it are archived and provided for deterministic independent recomputation. We release the full artifact bundle to enable reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi‑model, multi‑verifier replications and larger‑scale cost/latency studies to evaluate operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

References

[1] R. Cadenas, "Convergent Correctness in Stochastic Code Generation: A Generate‑Verify‑Repair Architecture for Deterministic Validation of Autonomous AI Coding Agents in Regulated Environments," SSRN, 2026. doi:10.2139/ssrn.6754899.

[2] M. Jouini, "Verifier‑First Evaluation of Agentic LLMs for Infrastructure‑as‑Code Generation," arXiv:2607.20478, 2026.

[3] A. Gupta, "Verifier Exploitation in NLI‑Guided Iterative Refinement: A Controlled Empirical Analysis," Research Square, 2026. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10187492/v1.

[4] T. Sah et al., "The Verifier Tax: Horizon Dependent Safety Success Tradeoffs in Tool Using LLM Agents," arXiv:2603.19328, 2026.

[5] M. Bilal, J. Crowcroft, R. Wang, X. Xu, and S. Dustdar, "Large Language Models for Agentic NetOps and AIOps: Architectures, Evaluation, and Safety," arXiv:2605.12729, 2026.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest). Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt‑5‑mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre‑lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics notes: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Harmful‑change mapping and reconstructability: the preregistered harmful‑change rules were frozen and the transformation artifact implementing the mapping is archived (see execution/transformation_manifest.json and the full artifact manifest execution/execution_manifest.json in the evidence bundle). Per‑episode raw traces and scoring artifacts required to reproduce all aggregated confirmatory and preregistered secondary statistics are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json; analysis/*.csv). The study followed the preregistered stopping rule; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled‑fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single‑model and single‑adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi‑model generality.
Simulator‑backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per‑fault‑class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large‑scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger‑scale study.

Verifier‑exploitation and long‑horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi‑verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful‑overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful‑overrepair aggregation; the per‑episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
